references.text: The next morning, Jacob took the stone he had placed under his head as a support, set it up as a pillar, poured oil over it, and called the place Bethel – a direct follow-up to the event in verse 11.
God commands Jacob to return to Bethel, the place where he lay down and met God in a dream, and Jacob builds an altar there.
Jacob meets God's angels at Mahanaim on his journey home, a parallel to the angels he saw in his dream when he stayed overnight at Bethel.
Jesus refers to Jacob's dream at Bethel when he says that the disciples will see heaven opened and God's angels ascending and descending over the Son of Man.
The book of Hebrews speaks of the faith of the patriarchs and their lives as foreigners in the promised land, living in tents – a parallel to Jacob's simple overnight stay under the open sky.
Direct continuation of the same event; shows the transformation of the stone from a sleeping pillow to a sacred memorial.
